title: Superdense Coding
summary: Two classical bits travel in one qubit when sender and receiver share a Bell pair.
objectives: Encode two classical bits on Alice's half of a Bell pair with Pauli gates
Decode both bits with a CNOT and a Hadamard gate and read them in the right order
Say why neither half of the pair carries any information about the message by itself
mission: Alice and Bob share a Bell pair: Alice holds qubit 1 and Bob holds qubit 0. Alice encodes the two-bit string `message` (the validator tries all four) by acting only on qubit 1, then sends that qubit to Bob, who decodes with gates that do not depend on the message. Reading |q1 q0⟩, the final state must be the message.
hints: What does Alice and Bob's shared resource look like, and which two gates created it in lesson 1.5? Build it first.
Alice's gates act on her qubit 1 and depend on the message, which is known when the circuit is built, so ordinary Python if statements work: Z if message[0] == "1", X if message[1] == "1".
Bob runs the pair-creation circuit backwards on both qubits: qc.cx(1, 0), then qc.h(1). That sends the four Bell states to |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩ and |11⟩ in |q1 q0⟩.

prediction.question: Someone intercepts qubit 1 on its way from Alice to Bob and measures it in the computational basis. What do they learn about the message?
options: Both bits, since qubit 1 is the qubit Alice encoded
Nothing: qubit 1 alone looks the same for every message
One bit, the one chosen by the X gate
prediction.explanation: Each Bell state has the reduced state I/2 on each qubit, so a measurement of qubit 1 alone gives 0 or 1 with probability 1/2 for all four messages. The message is in the correlations with Bob's qubit. The interceptor also spoils the protocol, because Bob no longer receives the Bell state.

challenge.mission: The shared pair is now |Ψ⁻⟩ = (|01⟩ − |10⟩)/√2 instead of |Φ⁺⟩: the circuit up to and including its first two-qubit gate must prepare it. Keep Bob's decoding (CNOT from 1 to 0, then H on qubit 1). Alice still acts only on qubit 1, and her gates, chosen from `message`, must make the final state |q1 q0⟩ equal to the message for all four messages.
hints: Bob's decoding sends Φ⁺ to 00, Φ⁻ to 10, Ψ⁺ to 01 and Ψ⁻ to 11. Which gate of Alice's turns |Ψ⁻⟩ into each of the four Bell states?
To prepare |Ψ⁻⟩, start with X on both qubits to get |11⟩, then H on qubit 0 and a CNOT from 0 to 1.
With no gate from Alice, Bob reads 11. Z on qubit 1 turns |Ψ⁻⟩ into |Ψ⁺⟩, and X turns it into |Φ⁻⟩. Work out which of the four combinations gives each message.
